sentences.text: The fossilized remains include the wing membrane, hair-like fibers, a long tail vane, and a head crest featuring a bony foundation with a large keratin extension.
Such a prominent head crest is an uncommon trait for early pterosaurs, which typically lack these elaborate structures in the fossil record.
This crest spanned the rear two-thirds of the skull and was strengthened by approximately twelve parallel ridges.
Scientists interpret a vertical pattern at the crest's base as evidence of the animal's original camouflage coloring.
The fibers were described as pinnate, resembling the base of bird down feathers and representing Stage II in feather evolution.
The genus Pterorhynchus was formally named in 2002 by Stephen Czerkas and Ji Qiang.
The type species for this genus is Pterorhynchus wellnhoferi.
The name translates to 'wing snout,' a reference to the tall crest situated on the animal's head.
The specific epithet wellnhoferi honors the German pterosaur researcher Peter Wellnhofer.
The holotype specimen was discovered in Chifeng within the Daohugou Beds.
Researchers proposed that the head crest served a primarily aerodynamic function.
The presence of these fibers suggests that pterosaur pycnofibers and dinosaur feathers were homologous structures.
Czerkas and Ji originally assigned Pterorhynchus to the family Rhamphorhynchidae.
However, a 2014 analysis by Andres and colleagues found Pterorhynchus to be a close relative of wukongopterids, placing it nearer to pterodactyloid pterosaurs.
Consequently, Andres and colleagues assigned Pterorhynchus to the group Darwinoptera.
The animal belongs to the suborder Rhamphorhynchoidea.
Pterorhynchus is part of the unranked family Darwinoptera.
The parent group of Pterorhynchus is Rhamphorhynchinae.
Ji assigned Pterorhynchus to the Yanliao Biota of the Haifanggou Formation during the Callovian stage.
Lü Junchang in 2007 suggested the animal lived in the later Tiaojishan Formation of the same stage.
Pterorhynchus lived between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago during the Callovian.
